newsitem.title: SYRIA: Palestinian rebel supports Tel Aviv bombs.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian rebel supports Tel Aviv bombs.

text.p: A Palestinian military commander said on Friday the bombings near Tel Aviv's central bus station which injured 13 people were a response for last week's attack on Arabs in the West Bank town of Hebron.

Brigadier Abu Ahmed Fu'ad, chief of the military department of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP), refused to confirm or deny his group's responsibility for Thursday's two bomb blasts.

"The Palestinian people are replying to the crime committed by Israel against the innocent people in Hebron. The bombings reflected our people's determination to continue resistance," Fu'ad told Reuters.

The blasts came one week after an off-duty Israeli soldier shot into a crowd of Palestinians in the West Bank town of Hebron, wounding seven Arabs in what he said was an attempt to stop Israel from carrying out its long-overdue troop redeployment from the town.
"We neither deny nor confirm our responsibility for the Tel Aviv blasts," Fu'ad said.

Israeli police said they did not know who dropped the bombs in garbage cans in Tel Aviv on Thursday night. They said forensic evidence pointed to a terrorist act but they could not rule out a criminal gangland attack.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu blamed "terrorists" and vowed to respond with "extreme severity" if the crude devices proved to have been planted by Arabs from areas under the control of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

The Damascus-based PFLP, led by George Habash, has wide support in the West Bank and Gaza Strip. It belongs to a 10-member radical Palestinian alliance which vowed to destroy the 1993 peace deal between Israel and the Palestinians.
It claimed responsibility for the killing in December of a Jewish settler and her son in the West Bank.
